annotations.name: ZSqrtNeg5
annotations.description: The ring Z[sqrt(-5)], represented as Zsqrtd(-5) from Mathlib

annotations.name: norm
annotations.description: The norm function N(a + b*sqrt(-5)) = a^2 + 5b^2, which is multiplicative and positive definite

annotations.name: no_norm_two
annotations.description: No element of Z[sqrt(-5)] has norm 2: the equation a^2 + 5b^2 = 2 has no integer solutions

annotations.name: no_norm_three
annotations.description: No element of Z[sqrt(-5)] has norm 3: the equation a^2 + 5b^2 = 3 has no integer solutions

annotations.name: unit_iff_norm_one
annotations.description: An element of Z[sqrt(-5)] is a unit if and only if its norm equals 1, characterizing units as exactly {+1, -1}

annotations.name: factorization_2
annotations.description: Second factorization: 6 = (1 + sqrt(-5)) * (1 - sqrt(-5)) in Z[sqrt(-5)]

annotations.name: two_irreducible
annotations.description: 2 is irreducible in Z[sqrt(-5)]: N(2)=4 and no element has norm 2, so 2 cannot factor nontrivially

annotations.name: three_irreducible
annotations.description: 3 is irreducible in Z[sqrt(-5)]: N(3)=9 and no element has norm 3

annotations.name: onePlus_irreducible
annotations.description: 1+sqrt(-5) is irreducible: N(1+sqrt(-5))=6 and no element has norm 2 or 3

annotations.name: oneMinus_irreducible
annotations.description: 1-sqrt(-5) is irreducible by the same norm argument

annotations.name: zsqrt_neg5_not_ufd
annotations.description: Main theorem: Z[sqrt(-5)] is NOT a unique factorization domain, proved by showing 2 is irreducible but not prime (2 divides (1+sqrt(-5))(1-sqrt(-5)) without dividing either factor)
